The best pick depends on the style you want. The reviews I read most often recommend these:

| Pick | Best for | Price | Battery | Water rating |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| [Shokz OpenDots 2](https://www.amazon.com/dp/B0GQ3H9YLF) | Best overall for most runners | $200 | 10 hrs (40 with case) | IP57 |
| [Shokz OpenRun Pro 2](https://www.amazon.com/dp/B0D2HKCMBP) | Best bone conduction, most awareness | $180 list, about $125 at [Best Buy or REI](https://www.wired.com/story/best-open-earbuds/) | 12 hrs | IP55 |
| [Bose Ultra Open Earbuds](https://www.bose.com/p/earbuds/bose-ultra-open-earbuds/ULT-HEADPHONEOPN.html) | Best sound, physical buttons | $199 (list $299) | 7 hrs | IPX4 |
| [Soundcore AeroClip 2](https://www.amazon.com/dp/B0HFJ7NVPB) | Long battery, good calls | $170 | 10–11 hrs | IPX5/IP55 |
| [JLab Flex Open](https://www.amazon.com/dp/B0D8K3WN1S) | Cheapest way to try open-ear | about $40 | 7 hrs | IPX4 or better, depending on retailer |

**Why these**
- **Shokz OpenDots 2:** [WIRED](https://www.wired.com/story/best-open-earbuds/) named it best overall. The reviewer wore it in rain and on the beach and submerged it without trouble. [Runner's World](https://www.runnersworld.com/gear/g63667125/best-open-ear-headphones-for-running/) calls it best for long runs and says the reviewer wore it on a 30-mile run. The buds work in either ear. Runner's World's reviewer felt a small zap when running in heavy rain, though, and found the volume only decent.
- **Shokz OpenRun Pro 2:** This is a neckband that combines bone conduction with small air-conduction speakers, so it sounds fuller than older bone-conduction models. WIRED says it's clearer in noisy places than most open earbuds. Runner's World warns that the band can get in the way of ponytails, winter hats and hoods, and that bass is thin.
- **Bose Ultra Open Earbuds:** Runner's World's top overall pick. WIRED praises the clear sound and the physical buttons, which are easier to use than touch controls when running. The speaker aims at your ear canal, so less sound leaks out. Runner's World also says Bose plans to release a new open-ear pair soon, so you may want to wait or watch for price drops.
- **Soundcore AeroClip 2:** Runner's World found the calls very clear and says 10 minutes of charging gives about 4 hours of playback. Bass is light. WIRED rated the original [Aeroclip](https://www.wired.com/story/best-open-earbuds/) as runner-up, but I couldn't find a review of the AeroClip 2 from them.
- **JLab Flex Open:** Less bass and detail, and touch controls only. It's a low-risk way to find out whether you like clip-ons.

**Other options**
- [Soundcore AeroFit 2](https://dealhunt.co/us-B0FW4PW4WY) is [SoundGuys](https://www.soundguys.com/best-open-ear-headphones-and-earbuds-115102/)' best budget pick. It has adjustable ear hooks, IP55 and about $80 at Amazon when SoundGuys checked. A [Dealectric page](https://dealectric.com/lab/V7/soundcore-aerofit-2) lists it at $129.99 at Soundcore's store, or $104 with code AFSC20. Dealectric earns a commission on that link, and the code excludes items already on sale. The Amazon price looks better, so check both before you buy.
- [Nothing Ear (Open)](https://dealhunt.co/us-B0DGLL5CWK), about $99, is SoundGuys' best overall. It has strong bass for this category and a good app, but only IP54 water resistance.
- [Sony LinkBuds Clip](https://www.amazon.com/dp/B0G4SKRJG7) has a voice-boost mode that suits podcasts and audiobooks, but bass is weak and it's only IPX4.

**How to choose**
- **Most awareness, or you run in a lot of rain:** OpenRun Pro 2.
- **Long runs:** OpenDots 2.
- **Best sound:** Bose.
- **Tight budget:** JLab Flex or AeroFit 2.

Fit varies with ear shape, so buy somewhere with an easy return policy. Open-ear headphones don't guarantee safety either, so keep the volume moderate.

 They come in three main styles: clip-on earbuds cuff onto the outer ear or clip over the shell, bone-conduction headphones rest on your cheekbones and behind your ear and send sound through vibration, and a few over-ear designs float speakers just off the ear.  The Best Open Earbuds I’ve Tested
 The best open earbuds let you hear your music while staying attuned to the world around you. After hundreds of hours of listening, I’ve decided these are the best.
 Courtesy of Bose 
 Save this story

 Open earbuds are the big new thing in headphone land. Unlike in-ear variants, open earbuds are like tiny speakers that rest on the ear and let outside sound in naturally, so you can fully hear the world around you. Some use a hook style that wraps around the back of your ear, while others are clip-ons that look more like statement-piece earrings. Style aside, they are excellent for anyone who finds traditional earbuds uncomfortable or wants full environmental awareness for activities like running, biking, or even just doing chores around the house.
 I've tested dozens of models since 2022, and while I still recommend having a pair of [noise-canceling earbuds](https://www.wired.com/gallery/best-noise-canceling-earbuds/), I also love open earbuds for specific use cases.
 For more headphone recommendations, check out our guides to the [Best Wireless Earbuds](https://www.wired.com/story/best-wireless-earbuds/), [Best Workout Headphones](https://www.wired.com/story/the-best-workout-headphones-and-earbuds/), and [Best Wireless Headphones](https://www.wired.com/gallery/best-wireless-headphones/).
